title: Vulnerability ops: SIEM field mapping and remediation playbook (RBAC v2 + evidence automation)
summary: Working playbook that ties scanner outputs to SIEM fields, defines remediation SLAs, and explains evidence automation and RBAC v2 ownership mapping for vuln handling.
body:
Purpose:
This document defines an operational playbook for handling vulnerability scanner outputs end-to-end: normalization, SIEM field mapping, automated evidence collection, RBAC v2 owner resolution, remediation tracking, and SLAs. It is intended for SecOps, SRE, and Eng teams who will receive and act on vuln tickets.

Principles:
- Single source of truth for vulnerability state lives in tracker (Linear/Jira) + evidence blob store.
- Normalize and dedupe scanner signals before creating tickets to avoid churn.
- Attach minimal, reproducible evidence to every remediation task.
- Map ownership through RBAC v2 tags on assets; default to platform-security queue if owner resolution fails.

1) Scanner output normalization (pre-ingest):
- Supported scanners: Trivy, Clair, Snyk, Dependabot, Internal kube-scan.
- Normalization steps: parse json -> map to canonical vuln_id (CVE, GHSA, internal fingerprint) -> compute fingerprint = sha256(vuln_id + package + version + asset_id) -> dedupe across scanners by fingerprint.
- Enrichment: join asset metadata from CMDB (service, owner_team, env, region), add runtime tag (k8s/pod/container or VM/instance).
- Severity mapping: map scanner severity to canonical (crit/high/med/low) using table in appendix. Include CVSSv3.score when available.

2) SIEM field mapping (ingest schema):
- Event fields to populate (canonical names): siem_event_type, timestamp, vuln_id, fingerprint, severity, cvss_v3, package_name, package_version, asset_id, asset_type, service_name, owner_team, owner_contact, env, region, proof_uri, scan_tool, scan_run_id, canonical_status, ticket_id, remediation_due, evidence_blob_uri
- Field rules: timestamp = ISO8601 UTC of scan finish; proof_uri = minimal repro steps or curl/wget commands; evidence_blob_uri = s3://sec-evidence/{ticket_id}/{artifact}.gz or pre-signed URL for 7d.
- SIEM ingest method: preferred = https/http bulk JSON API with index mapping; fallback = syslog TLS over port 6514.
- Normalized event type: vulnerabilty.finding. Use following tags: tag:asset:service, tag:severity:critical/high/med/low, tag:env:prod/staging/dev.

3) RBAC v2 owner resolution and defaulting:
- Primary owner lookup order: asset metadata.owner_team -> service tags (git repo CODEOWNERS) -> workload labels (k8s team) -> infra owner.
- If owner_team resolves to a team alias, map to team Slack channel and escalation contact using team directory table.
- RBAC v2 role required to acknowledge ticket: sec:vuln-ack or sec:platform-owner. Ticket assignment should include role hints.
- If unresolved within 24h (non-prod) or 12h (prod critical), auto-assign to security-oncall and create high-priority PagerDuty incident.

4) Remediation tracking and SLAs:
- SLA definitions (business):
  - critical (RCE, Linux kernel panic, active exploit): 48 hours to remediation (fix or mitigated fallback) and 24 hours to initial acknowledgement.
  - high (auth bypass, privilege escalation potential): 7 days to remediation, 48 hours to acknowledgement.
  - medium (info leak, moderate risk): 30 days to remediation, 7 days to acknowledgement.
  - low (cosmetic / unlikely exploit): 90 days to remediation, 14 days to acknowledgement.
- Ticket lifecycle states: triaged -> in_progress -> awaiting_verification -> verified -> closed. Use workflow webhooks to update SIEM canonical_status.
- Required evidence per state transition:
  - on in_progress: include proposed fix summary and MR/PR link; include any workaround applied.
  - on awaiting_verification: include test plan, patch commit hash, image digest or package artifact, CI run id.
  - on verified: attach verification logs and SIEM event showing absence of previously observed behavior.

5) Evidence automation pipeline (recommended implementation):
- Steps: scanner -> normalization lambda -> enrich with CMDB -> write normalized event to SIEM and create ticket via issue API -> attach evidence placeholder (artifact URI) -> kick off auto-collect job that runs ephemeral repro job to capture minimal logs and system state -> upload gzipped evidence to blob store and update ticket with evidence_blob_uri.
- Automation notes: evidence artifacts should be immutable and signed (sha256). Retention default 90 days; extendable via compliance request.
- Access controls: evidence blob store objects must inherit RBAC v2 ACLs; only security and ticket assignees get read access by default.

6) SIEM alert tuning and correlation rules:
- Create correlation rules that combine: repeated fingerprint across assets in prod within 24h -> escalate to high.
- Enrich SIEM with deployment metadata (image digest, commit SHA) for faster triage.
- Add rule: known false-positive list (hash list) to suppress noisy scanner signals. Maintain false-positive list in repo security/false-positives.yaml.

7) Operational play actions (runbook snippets):
- On new critical vuln ingestion: 1) triage within 1 hour, 2) confirm exploitability via quick repro (sandbox), 3) open hotfix PR and target emergency rollout channel, 4) notify customers if customer-impacting via CS template.
- On high/untriaged backlog growth > 15% week-over-week: allocate rotation from platform teams for 2-week remediation sprint.

Appendix: examples and mappings
- Example normalized SIEM event (fields listed above).
- Severity mapping example: Trivy CRITICAL -> critical; Snyk HIGH -> high; Dependabot MODERATE -> medium.
- Ticket template (Linear/Jira): title = [vuln] {vuln_id} {service_name} {env} {severity}; description = scanner details, repro steps, asset link, proposed fix, SLA deadline.
- Quick lookup commands for evidence reproduction: kubectl -n {ns} logs -c {container} {pod} | gzip -c > evidence.gz; curl -X GET "{service}/healthz?verbose=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" > proof.json

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm retention policy for evidence beyond 90 days for enterprise customers.
- Define exact RBAC v2 role binding naming convention for service-level owners (proposal: service:{service_name}:owner).
- Decide whether to include pre-signed evidence URLs in SIEM events (current plan: yes, 7d expiry).

Owners and next steps:
- Primary doc owner: Asha Patel (secops).
- Action items: implement normalization lambda (ENG infra), add SIEM ingest mapping (SRE/observability), wire ticket creation template (Security automation).
